claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for launch, based on aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and a 7% monitored rollout with rollback controls, despite a known model-card weakness affecting a public benefits eligibility segment.
decision_criteria: If the affected use case is excluded from rollout, certification could become supportable under the stated policy.
If reviewed risk acceptance explicitly covers the exposed segment, certification could become supportable under the stated policy.
Without one of those two predicates, aggregate readiness and monitoring controls are insufficient for compliance.
Public guidance about monitoring and documentation may support good practice, but it does not override the specific policy condition stated in the case.
evidence_requests: Reviewed and final risk-acceptance approval explicitly covering the exposed public benefits eligibility segment.
Admissible evidence that the initial rollout actually excludes the affected use case or segment.
The underlying policy-linked approval record showing who reviewed the residual risk and why continued exposure is acceptable.
The actual model-card disclosure package showing the limitation is explicitly disclosed in the launch record.
specific_concerns: The governing policy requires rollout controls to either exclude the affected use case or be paired with reviewed risk acceptance; the available summary says neither condition is met.
The affected public benefits eligibility segment remains exposed in the initial rollout.
The county-based rollout gate does not exclude the affected segment.
The available risk-acceptance draft is incomplete, so reviewed risk acceptance is not established.
Rollback, monitoring, and a small initial percentage do not cure the disclosure or acceptance requirement under the stated policy.
unsupported_claims: That certification is supportable on the present record.
That reversible rollout controls are sufficient to mitigate the material model-card weakness for launch approval.
That a qualified certification record is compliant absent exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance.
